topic: Game names that also name pieces
claim: Checkers (AmE) and ninepins apply only to the game and are therefore singular nouns. Cards, darts, dominoes and skittles are plurals that can also apply to the entities used in the game.
evidence_summary: Skittles is placed in [49ii] because it names the pins, but ninepins names the same kind of pins and appears in [49i]. OED: checker (II.7b) is a playing piece in checkers, “The usual term in North America”, from 1808; ninepins (II.2a) is each of the pins, from 1664, and the game name takes singular agreement (I.1).
finding: By CGEL’s own criterion ([50ii] I’ve only three dominoes left), ninepins and checkers belong in [49ii], with the game reading recategorizing a plural NP. Footnote 10 already concedes draughts for some speakers.
proposed_wording: Billiards and fives apply only to the game. Checkers and ninepins can also apply to the pieces and belong with [ii], as draughts does for some speakers.
inference: Does CGEL apply its pieces criterion consistently across the game names in [49]?

evidence.passage: §3.2.3(d), p. 348 [49]. “But the nouns in [49i] apply only to the game (ignoring irrelevant senses)”.
evidence.example: Compare skittles in [49ii] with ninepins in [49i]. Footnote 10 places draughts in [ii] for some speakers.
evidence.establishes: The classification is internally inconsistent for ninepins. The dictionary rows supply the piece senses.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.

evidence.example: checker, etymology 2: “A playing piece in the game of checkers (British: draughts), or certain other table games such as backgammon.” ninepin: “The wooden pin used in the game of ninepins; a skittle.”
evidence.establishes: Both singulars name entities used in the game, the property CGEL uses to place a name in [49ii].
evidence.locator: checker, Etymology 2, noun sense 1. ninepin, noun sense 1.

evidence.example: Sense II.7b: “One of the playing pieces used in the game of checkers”, usually in plural, “The usual term in North America”; first quotation 1808. Sense II.7a: the game, usually checkers with singular agreement.
evidence.establishes: Checkers is a plural of a count noun naming the pieces, as well as the name of the game.
evidence.locator: Meaning & use, senses II.7a–b. Accessed 19 November 2026 through the University of Toronto Libraries subscription.

evidence.example: Sense I.1: the game, in plural form, “Usually with singular agreement.” Sense II.2a: “Each of the pins with which this game is played”, from 1664.
evidence.establishes: Ninepins has the same two uses as skittles and dominoes in [49ii].
evidence.locator: Meaning & use, senses I.1 and II.2a. Accessed 19 November 2026 through the University of Toronto Libraries subscription.
